title: Rematch round 1, Skippy Core's coder: lost to Haiku's round 1 train
model: Skippy Core's coder (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MTP, Q8) as a vanilla agent (Claude Code with purple's system prompt, an empty setup, effort high, a 131K window) plus purple's generic help: eyes (Core's vision model describes the pictures it opens) and the stop gate's work check (MineBench's runtime as the checker, the renderer as the viewer, an 80K output-token budget)
verdict: Lost to Haiku's head-to-head round 1 train (blind judge, high confidence). The help worked as built: the stop gate showed it its build three times and nudged it once on the budget, and it saw every picture through Core's vision model, rebuilding after each look: 41 minutes and 92 turns, against 12 minutes before. But the vision model told it the train was recognizable, and the judge didn't agree: a long train on a raised grey platform over a tan track (black-and-yellow body, a brown wagon, three white-and-red boxcars, trees, smoke puffs) with a big yellow ring sitting right on top of the locomotive, no wheels or smokestack the judge could see, cars that look like boxes on a slab, and striped grass with black gaps. Haiku's: the steam locomotive, three coaches on rails, a station and a water tower.
